bepridil inhibits recombinant Cav3.2 (CACNA1H) T-type current stably expressed in human HEK-293 cells, patch clamp, voltage-dependent tonic block, IC50 0.4 umol/l at a holding potential of -70 mV and 10.6 umol/l at -100 mV (26-fold), steady-state inactivation and conductance curves shifted hyperpolarised by 10 umol/l, no use-dependent block and no effect on recovery from inactivation; FUNCTIONAL electrophysiology, not binding; PubMed:15855830 (Pharmacology 2005;74, doi 10.1159/000085329), abstract read 2026-11-02, title and sentences 1-5; the abstract does not state the species of the Cav3.2 clone; DrugCentral 2027 separately records bepridil against human CACNA1H / UniProt O95180 as a SINGLE protein, which is a species- and subunit-resolved TARGET ASSIGNMENT and not an independent confirmation of anything (drug.target.interaction.tsv, ORGANISM Homo sapiens); that DrugCentral row's ACTION_TYPE BLOCKER has MOA_SOURCE CHEMBL (action_origin_class SHARED) so it is NOT an independent confirmation of the direction, and its ACT_TYPE Ki 5.149 from WOMBAT-PK is a BINDING measure that licenses no direction; ChEMBL_37 holds no activity for CHEMBL1008 on CHEMBL1859 (CACNA1H single protein) or CHEMBL2362995 (T-type family), and GtoPdb 2026.3.1 lists bepridil (ligand 2337) on KNa1.1 and Kv7.4 only, so those two sources are silent rather than negative; the ChEMBL group mechanism this answers cites PubMed:10792039, a troponin-C structure paper, so PubMed:15855830 is independent of the module's own input; CACNA1H ONLY - no Cav3.1 (CACNA1G) or Cav3.3 (CACNA1I) value was found, and this row licenses no direction on them; says nothing about benefit, safety or any effect in a WWOX-deficient system
